title: Quick check: Running and Building a React Application

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Running and Building a React Application”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Development mode must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Development mode must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Running and Building a React Application: Development mode must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Development mode?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Running and Building a React Application: Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Running and Building a React Application” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Running and Building a React Application: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
